sentences.text: This part adds up the state, the voice-mail plan and some usage figures with fixed weights: a voice-mail plan lowers a typical customer's chance of leaving from about 3% to about 1%, and a higher evening charge raises it steadily, from about 2% at 11.76 to about 5% at 22.57 US dollars.

More night-time minutes (about 2% at 136 to about 4% at 264 minutes) and more daytime calls (about 3% at 75 to about 4% at 125 calls) raise it steadily, and a higher night-time charge lowers it steadily by less than a point.

Through it, the state moves the chance from about 3% in West Virginia to about 12% in California, about 9% in Washington and about 7% in Maine and New Jersey, and down to about 2% in Colorado and about 1% in Hawaii and Vermont (41 to 122 training customers per state; the full list is in the technical detail).

The daytime charge counts more with an evening charge above 17.12 US dollars, adding nothing until about 33.67 US dollars, then steadily: from about 3% to about 12% between 19.07 and 42.40 US dollars, against about 3% to about 4% with a lower evening charge.
This part reads daytime minutes alone: they add nothing until about 215 minutes, then raise the chance steadily, from about 3% to about 9% between 0 and 271 minutes for a typical customer.
